title: What happens when the number gets ten times smaller?
description: A hundred and thirty two is divided by four, and the same division is done again with the number divided by ten, a hundred and a thousand. Each time the answer from the first division is divided by the same power of ten. Multiplying back checks one answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the number being divided is divided by ten, a hundred or a thousand, the answer is divided by the same amount. Watch for students who divide again from the start and slip with the point.

video_script.why: The child can divide a whole number by four but loses the decimal point when the number is a decimal.
video_script.substitution: The number is a hundred and thirty two divided by ten, a hundred or a thousand, so the answer is thirty three divided by the same amount.
video_script.anchor: A hundred and thirty two, thirteen point two, one point three two and zero point one three two, each divided by four
video_script.payoff_line: Zero point one three two divided by four is zero point zero three three.

final_answer.spoken: thirty three, three point three, zero point three three and zero point zero three three

video_script.design: The four divisions stay on the board; the whole number division is done once and the point moves one, two and three places left.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four divisions side by side: 132 ÷ 4, 13.2 ÷ 4, 1.32 ÷ 4, 0.132 ÷ 4, each with an empty answer box
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing by four.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two numbers are a hundred and thirty two and thirteen point two.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next two are one point three two and zero point one three two. Each is divided by four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is each quotient?

beats.on_screen: the four divisions and their empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 132, 13.2, 1.32, 0.132 in a row; the decimal point slides one place left each time, and each number is 132 divided by 10, 100 or 1000

marks.row: the four numbers are lined up with their decimal points
marks.slide: the point slides one place left each time, so each number is ten times smaller

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. Divide the whole number first.
<bookmark mark='slide'/>Each number after it is ten times smaller than the one before. Each answer is ten times smaller too.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four numbers to be divided by four. A hundred and thirty two, thirteen point two, one point three two and zero point one three two.

marks.find: the four answer boxes are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the quotient of each division.

marks.s1b: 33 × 4 = 132 is written beside it and 33 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, a hundred and thirty two divided by four.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Thirty three times four is a hundred and thirty two, so the answer is thirty three.

marks.s2b: 33 ÷ 10 is written and the point slides one place left to give 3.3

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, thirteen point two is a hundred and thirty two divided by ten.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Divide thirty three by ten, and we get three point three.

marks.s3b: 33 ÷ 100 is written and the point slides two places left to give 0.33

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, one point three two is a hundred and thirty two divided by a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Divide thirty three by a hundred, and we get zero point three three.

marks.s4b: 33 ÷ 1000 is written with the decimal left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, zero point one three two is a hundred and thirty two divided by a thousand.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Divide thirty three by a thousand. The point slides three places left.

marks.s5b: the product 1.32 is matched with the number in 1.32 ÷ 4

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, check by multiplying back. Zero point three three times four is one point three two.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>That matches the number we began with.

marks.rest: the other three answers are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Zero point one three two divided by four is zero point zero three three.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other three are thirty three, three point three and zero point three three.
